subject: Re: Request for binding no-train + KMS residency / conditional escrow details
messages:
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@mednova.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: brian.cole@mednova.com
Date: 2026-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redlines: explicit no-train + KMS residency proof

Irene / team,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are our redlines (MedNova_DPA_redlines_2026-08-04.pdf) — the two items blocking legal/procurement sign-off are: 1) an explicit, contractually-binding no-training commitment for customer input (and a short definition of what that excludes), and 2) operational proof we can rely on for KMS residency (customer-controlled keys, onshore key management for US workloads).

Concretely: we need language that says Redwood will not use MedNova transactional data to improve models (no adaptive training or model tuning), plus evidence we can review that shows where keys live and how access is logged. If you can propose acceptable operational evidence (runbook, attestation, sample audit logs) and an escrow/conditional-release mechanism for derivatives in a breach scenario, that would help us move forward quickly.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Offer a no-train commitment limited to PII and transaction payloads (we need to understand the carveouts)
- Provide KMS residency with customer-managed keys for US region (or a documented onshore key-split approach)
- Describe conditional escrow terms (when derivatives might be released to us or an escrow agent)

We've attached the redlines. Happy to schedule a short call if helpful.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Kumar
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security — MedNova Health

Attachments: MedNova_DPA_redlines_2026-08-04.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@mednova.com>, brian.cole@mednova.com
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: explicit no-train + KMS residency proof

Aisha — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. High-level response and next steps below. I'll loop in ops/crypto for the technical evidence.

Summary of what Redwood can offer (initial):
- No-train commitment: Redwood can agree to a contractual prohibition on using MedNova production inputs to continuously train or fine-tune our shared models. We need to define the scope (e.g., exclude telemetry/aggregate safety signals and public data). We propose specific wording in a redline (attached).
- KMS residency / CMK: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for the US region via our KMS integration. For certain deployment types we can provide a key-split / onshore wrapping design as an alternative.
- Conditional escrow for derivatives: We are open to a narrowly scoped conditional-escrow mechanism (release to customer or neutral escrow agent only upon verified, narrowly-defined breach or legal order). We need to work through triggers and the operational process.

Internal action items: David / Kimberly — can you confirm the evidence artifacts we can provide (runbook, sample logs, attestation letter) and whether the key-split option meets onshore residency constraints?

Proposed next step: We will prepare Redwood_DPA_v4_redlines.pdf with suggested language + an ops evidence pack (list of files). Happy to join a 30-min call to walk through.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Irene / Kimberly — quick ops note to support the response to MedNova.

What we can provide today as evidence:
- Attestation letter (signed) describing the no-train operational control and our policy enforcement points.
- Sample audit logs showing KMS wrap/unwrap events for a synthetic customer key (redacted), including timestamps and actor IDs.
- Runbook excerpt describing key lifecycle and on-call escalation.
- Subprocessors list (current snapshot) — note some infra subprocessors are cloud regions and logging services; we can mark which ones process keys vs. model telemetry.

KMS approaches we can offer:
1) Customer-managed key via cloud KMS (BYOK): customer controls master key; our service requests wrapped keys and cannot unwrap without the cloud KMS permission. This meets most residency asks when keys are provisioned in the US.
2) Key-split design: we hold a wrapped shard, customer holds the other shard in their KMS; both are required for unwrapping. We can provide an architectural diagram and proof-of-concept logs. This is slightly higher ops overhead but provides an extra residency/control property.

Conditional escrow: we can agree to escrow only for derivative model artifacts explicitly generated from MedNova inputs and only under strict triggers (court order, verified breach of contract). The escrow mechanism would be documented and include chain-of-custody and an independent agent.

I'll attach a short ops note with what artifacts we can share for review.

-David
David Kim
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-ops-note.txt

Aisha / Brian — thanks for the patience while we pulled the ops details together. Attached is a draft redline package (Redwood_DPA_v4_redlines.pdf) and our current subprocessors snapshot (subprocessors_list_2026-08.csv). Key points / proposed commitments below.

1) Contract language (summary):
- Binding no-train: Redwood will not use MedNova customer inputs or customer-identifying metadata to train, fine-tune, or adapt any models used to serve MedNova, except for aggregated safety telemetry that cannot be reverse-engineered. Proposed redline includes a short definition and examples.
- Derivatives escrow: Redwood will not transfer model derivatives attributable to MedNova except under narrow triggers (finalized court order or verified contractual breach). In such a case we propose release to a neutral escrow agent only after a documented review and customer notification timeline.

2) Operational evidence we will provide prior to signing (for review only):
- Signed attestation describing the no-train control points.
- Sample KMS audit logs (redacted) showing wrap/unwrap events.
- Architecture diagram of the key-split option and runbook excerpt.
- Subprocessor inventory with processing purpose tags.

3) KMS residency options:
- BYOK provisioned in US region (recommended).
- Key-split option (extra control, slightly higher onboarding time).

Next steps we propose:
- We upload the redlines to DocuSign for legal review (https://app.docusign.com/mednova/redwood-dpa-v4).
- MedNova legal to review the redlines and ops artifacts; suggest a single 30-min alignment call if there are open carveouts.

If that sounds acceptable, I'll send the DocuSign package and drop the attachments into the secure review folder.

Regards,
Irene
Head of Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
